# What does a meristem cell look like?

<!-- STEP id="small-thin" -->
## Small, with a thin wall
Zoom in on one cell near the root tip, and put a permanent cell from farther back beside it. The meristem cell is small, and its cell wall is thin.

<!-- STEP id="nucleus" -->
## A large nucleus and dense cytoplasm
It has a large, prominent nucleus. Its cytoplasm is dense and full of organelles, the small working parts of a cell that you met in an earlier chapter, on cells.

<!-- STEP id="vacuole" -->
## Vacuoles generally absent
In a meristem cell, vacuoles are generally absent. The permanent cell beside it is much bigger, and a large vacuole fills most of it.

<!-- STEP id="packed" -->
## Tightly packed
Meristem cells are tightly packed, with little or no intercellular space. Intercellular space means the gaps between neighbouring cells.

<!-- STEP id="allow" -->
## Built for division
Together, these features suit a cell whose work is to divide.

**These features allow meristem cells to divide continuously and rapidly.**
